title: Disembodied Machine Learning: On the Illusion of Objectivity in NLP

bias_targets.methodology: Conceptual evaluation using feminist Science and Technology Studies (STS) to critique patriarchal assumptions in machine translation (e.g., observing the default translation of gender-neutral English terms like 'doctor' and 'nurse' to gender-marked German equivalents).

Theoretical critique of abusive language detection datasets, highlighting how universally applied 'objective' labels mischaracterize African-American English (such as in-group n-word usage) by imposing a disembodied, white perspective of respectability.

Qualitative analysis of text simplification datasets, arguing that establishing universal 'gold' labels for text difficulty fails to account for the subjective embodiments and needs of varying user groups, such as L2 language learners and individuals with dyslexia.
